quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Imagine someone sitting silently in a meeting, never offering an idea.
quests.explanation: Passive is correct — it means not taking an active part, accepting without acting, the opposite of active.
quests.textToSpeak: Try to stay *active* by taking a short walk every evening.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: That's watching from the sidelines instead of joining the game.
quests.explanation: Not taking part, just accepting things as they happen, is passive, the reverse of active.
quests.textToSpeak: Our teacher encourages *active* participation during discussions.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Consider someone who lets things happen without ever taking part.
quests.explanation: Active means taking part and doing things; passive, its opposite, means simply letting things happen.
quests.textToSpeak: She takes an *active* role in every team meeting.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Envision a flight with two layovers before finally reaching its destination.
quests.explanation: Indirect is the word here — it means not straightforward, going through another route, the opposite of direct.
quests.textToSpeak: We booked a *direct* flight to avoid a long layover.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: This is an answer that dances around the real question instead of stating it.
quests.explanation: Good call. Not straightforward, going through another route, is indirect, the reverse of direct.
quests.textToSpeak: My uncle prefers to give *direct* answers instead of hints.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Call to mind a road that winds through five other towns to get where you're going.
quests.explanation: Direct means going straight to the point; indirect, its opposite, means taking a roundabout path.
quests.textToSpeak: The manager gave a *direct* explanation for the price increase.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Think of a class you're legally required to attend, no exceptions.
quests.explanation: Exactly — compulsory. It means required by law or rule, not optional, the opposite of voluntary.
quests.textToSpeak: Bringing a dish to the potluck is *voluntary*, not required.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: It's a safety inspection every driver must pass by law.
quests.explanation: Required by rule, with no choice involved, is compulsory, the reverse of voluntary.
quests.textToSpeak: Updating the app is *voluntary* for now, but required next month.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Picture a form you have no choice but to fill out.
quests.explanation: Voluntary means optional, done by choice; compulsory, its opposite, means required, with no choice at all.
quests.textToSpeak: The flu vaccine at our office is *voluntary* this year.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Imagine a product shipped in from a factory overseas.
quests.explanation: Foreign is right here — it means from or relating to another country, the opposite of domestic.
quests.textToSpeak: The film festival features both *domestic* and international movies.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: That's a language you'd hear on a trip to another country.
quests.explanation: Sharp answer. From or relating to another country is foreign, the reverse of domestic.
quests.textToSpeak: We usually buy *domestic* fruit instead of imported ones.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Consider a passport stamped in a country you don't call home.
quests.explanation: Domestic means from your own country; foreign, its opposite, means from somewhere else.
quests.textToSpeak: The university welcomes both *domestic* and exchange students.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Envision a wool sweater pulled straight from an accidentally hot wash.
quests.explanation: Shrink is correct — it means to become smaller in size or amount, the opposite of expand.
quests.textToSpeak: The company plans to *expand* into two new cities next year.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: This is a company closing branches instead of opening new ones.
quests.explanation: Becoming smaller in size or amount is to shrink, the reverse of expand.
quests.textToSpeak: Budget airlines continue to *expand* their routes across Europe.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Call to mind a balloon slowly losing air until it's half its size.
quests.explanation: Expand means to grow larger; shrink, its opposite, means to become smaller.
quests.textToSpeak: Our family business slowly began to *expand* after the first year.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Think of a wrecking ball swinging into the side of an old building.
quests.explanation: Demolish is the word here — it means to completely destroy a building, the opposite of construct.
quests.textToSpeak: Workers will *construct* a new shopping center downtown.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: It's a bulldozer flattening a house to make way for something new.
quests.explanation: Completely destroying a building or structure is to demolish, the reverse of construct.
quests.textToSpeak: The city plans to *construct* a public market near the harbor.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Picture workers tearing down walls instead of putting them up.
quests.explanation: Construct means to build something; demolish, its opposite, means to tear it down.
quests.textToSpeak: Engineers will *construct* a new data center outside the city.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Imagine an application stamped 'denied' and sent straight back.
quests.explanation: That's right — reject. It means to refuse to accept something, the opposite of approve.
quests.textToSpeak: The agency will *approve* the new medicine after more testing.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: That's a manuscript a publisher decides not to print.
quests.explanation: Well judged. Refusing to accept or agree to something is to reject, the reverse of approve.
quests.textToSpeak: The studio decided to *approve* the sequel's script.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Consider an idea turned down flat during a meeting.
quests.explanation: Approve means to accept and agree to something; reject, its opposite, means to turn it down.
quests.textToSpeak: My landlord had to *approve* the request before we could repaint.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Envision a guest list with your name crossed off on purpose.
quests.explanation: Exclude is right here — it means to leave something out, not include it, the opposite of include.
quests.textToSpeak: The syllabus will *include* two extra chapters this semester.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: This is a recipe that deliberately leaves out one key ingredient.
quests.explanation: Leaving something out on purpose is to exclude, the reverse of include.
quests.textToSpeak: The budget report should *include* last month's expenses.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Call to mind a report that leaves an entire section out completely.
quests.explanation: Include means to add something in; exclude, its opposite, means to leave it out.
quests.textToSpeak: The tour package will *include* breakfast every morning.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Think of someone telling you your idea will never work, so don't even try.
quests.explanation: Precisely — discourage. It means to make someone less willing to do something, the opposite of encourage.
quests.textToSpeak: My parents always *encourage* us to try new hobbies.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: It's a steep price that makes people think twice before buying.
quests.explanation: Good ear. Making someone less willing to try something is to discourage, the reverse of encourage.
quests.textToSpeak: The discount is meant to *encourage* customers to buy in bulk.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Picture a coach who convinces a player to just give up.
quests.explanation: Encourage means to inspire someone to act; discourage, its opposite, means to talk them out of it.
quests.textToSpeak: Nutritionists *encourage* eating more vegetables every day.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Imagine an employee cleaning out their desk after a difficult meeting with HR.
quests.explanation: Fire is the word here — it means to end someone's employment, the opposite of hire.
quests.textToSpeak: The startup plans to *hire* five new developers this month.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: That's what happens when a company lets a worker go for good.
quests.explanation: Ending someone's employment is to fire, the reverse of hire.
quests.textToSpeak: The hospital will *hire* more nurses for the night shift.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Consider handing back a badge and keys on your very last day.
quests.explanation: Hire means to bring someone on for a job; fire, its opposite, means to let them go.
quests.textToSpeak: The studio decided to *hire* a new director for the sequel.
